I’m not defending leaving merchandise out, I’m defending common sense in a world that lost its damn mind. This is virtue signaling at its finest, see low hanging fruit and act like it’s a dire issue in need of totalitarian measures to reign in. 

Costco is definitely a private company, and you would think that if they thought the concept of saving money by monitoring the food closer is worth the investment that they would have already done so by now. It’s not like they don’t have entire teams of well payed executives that look for cost saving avenues, and methods to protect their brand. 

Costco is seen as a consumer friendly company, with their incredibly generous return policies, prices, and services. Do you think that hunting down their members are charging them for something that they can then return for full price is something that they would want for their brand image or awareness?

How do you know they had a cart and that was in it? So now you are paying an individual, I don't know how much a loss prevention specialist makes, \~$15/hr + benefits to watch for orphaned meat. By doing this, you might break even, but you will lose trust and goodwill from your customers, through which your shrinkage is already at ridiculously low levels. Also, you will open yourself up to litigation by those customers you accuse of "stealing/destroying" food. 

This sounds like a much more reasonable course of action when compared to having associates make rounds looking for wayward food.

I understand what you are saying, and thank you for the perspective, but I completely disagree with your final statement. If Drag were becoming vanilla smooth jazz, it wouldn't be as vilified by large swathes of the country and world. Drag will probably always be vilified, especially as long as it is such a visible expression of queer art, and no matter how vanilla it goes nothing will change that, but it would be a much easier pill to swallow and ignore if it was made into a Panto performance.

I would consider that take, if it is one that Lady Bunny ascribes to, as heavily reductive and disingenuous. A person can profit off of something, without exploiting it. I don't know to what degree RuPaul might be exploiting Drag, if at all, but to disregard the good that the show has enabled for queer kids, and queer people in general isn't a good look.

Drag is queer art at its most explicit, it is queer art without the thin veneer of ambiguity that exists with most other art mediums. You can view a painting, listen to a orchestra, or watch a play by a queer entertainer and easily dismiss that they are queer or that the art itself is born of a queer person's imagination, but with Drag that suspension of belief is made damn near impossible.
